title: Transient capacity hedger and adjustable utilization sampler
author: Asha Khatri
release_notes: Adds a transient capacity hedger to smooth short-lived bursts across dedicated pools and an adjustable utilization sampler that produces compact telemetry for per-tenant utilization profiling. Default defaults kept conservative; feature gated behind 'transient_hedge' flag for safe rollout.
body: Motivation: Dedicated fleets see frequent short-lived microbursts that cause oscillatory autoscaling and noisy unit economics reporting. Current autoscalers either overcommit to handle spikes (wasting cost) or underreact (violating throughput SLAs). This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a transient capacity hedger that temporarily borrows a small fraction of unallocated reservoir across pool slices to satisfy microbursts without triggering full scale-ups, and (2) an adjustable utilization sampler that creates compact, high-fidelity telemetry for downstream decision-making and billing smoothing. Design summary: - Hedger controller: new controller (TransientHedger) runs alongside the provisioner and watches per-pool short-window utilization; when a microburst is detected it loans a credit from a sub-reservoir governed by hedge_window_ms and hedge_fraction. Credits decay with an exponential half-life to avoid permanent leakage. - Safety and fairness: loans are capped per-tenant and per-pool. A 'safety_floor' ensures the hedger cannot deplete emergency reserve. Hedger exposes signals for fallback (hedge_exhausted) so request router can fall back to soft-degraded models. - Adjustable Utilization Sampler: workload-aware sampler that emits sketches (exponential buckets + reservoir sampling) per-tenant for short/medium windows; supports configurable resolution and sample retention. Sampler output feeds autoscaler heuristics and the Console telemetry surface. - Configs and rollout: new DedicatedCapacityPolicy fields: transient_hedge.enabled, transient_hedge.hedge_fraction (default 0.10), transient_hedge.hedge_window_ms (default 15000), transient_hedge.decay_half_life_ms (60000), sampler.window_seconds, sampler.resolution. Feature gated behind a runtime flag and syncable through console. Checklist: - [x] Hedger algorithm and controller implemented - [x] Conservative defaults and feature gate - [x] Unit tests for hedging math and decay - [x] Integration test exercising burst without scale-up - [x] Telemetry exporter and Console chart hooks - [x] Documentation and FAQ entry - [x] Canary rollout in perf lab (see benchmark results) Commits summary: - add: transient hedger controller, hedger state machine, tests - add: utilization sampler, sketch encoder and exporter - feat: expose new DedicatedCapacityPolicy fields and runtime flags - fix: race in allocator when hedger returns credits - perf: microbench harness and acceptance test - docs: console guide and FAQ Changed areas (high level): - core/provisioner/hedger_controller.go (new) - core/allocator/borrower.go (small surface changes to accept temporary credits) - telemetry/sampler/sketch.go and telemetry/exporter/hedge_metrics.go - api/dedicated_policy.proto (policy fields) - console/frontend/src/pages/dedicated/HedgeOverview.tsx (new chart) - tests/integration/hedge_burst_test.go - tests/unit/hedger_math_test.go - ci/config/canary-perf.yml (canary run) Review conversation summary: Initial review flagged two concerns: 1) Default hedge_fraction numeric value and unit tests flakiness that surfaced when decay timer races occurred in CI; 2) Metric cardinality for sampler sketches (risk of high cardinality with per-tenant tags). Reviewer feedback: - Liam: asked to reduce default hedge_fraction from 0.15 to 0.10 and add explicit guardrails for negative credit accounting; requested clearer metric labels to avoid per-tenant explosion. - Marina: requested an integration test that simulates concurrent hedger loan/return under preemption; noted a concurrency bug in borrower.go that could double-return credits in stress. - Diego: asked for documentation on fallbacks and a Console UX stub for operators to toggle the feature. Author replies/action: - Lowered default hedge_fraction to 0.10, added safety_floor checks, and a single-owner return semaphore to borrower.go; added a sampler label aggregation (tenant_id_isolated -> tenant_group) to bound cardinality; added integration scenario that reproduces preemption path. - Fixed unit test deterministic timers by injecting a clock interface; added more robust mocks for allocator. CI summary: - Initial CI run (linux/unit + go vet + fmt) passed; integration CI failed on hedger race in borrower return (flaky test). - Reproduced locally, fixed race by adding atomic state and stricter ownership semantics; re-ran canary perf job (ci/config/canary-perf.yml) against benchmark lab; latency and throughput regressions within 2% and 0.5% cost delta respectively. - Final CI run: all checks passed (unit, integration, e2e-canary, lint). Observability and metrics: - New metrics: redwood.dedicated.hedger.loans_total, .loans_failed, .loans_repaid, .hedge_exhausted_count, .util_sampler.sketch_count - Sampler emits compressed sketch payloads and a hashed tenant_group to the Console; retention defaults to 7 days for high-res windows. Performance notes: - Canary indicates the hedger reduces scale-up events by ~38% for 95th percentile microbursts in benchmark-lab synthetic workload (short spikes with <10s tail). - Overhead: hedger controller CPU < 0.6% of the provisioner service under 1k pools. Rollout plan: - Feature-gated default off for managed customers; enable for internal perf canaries and opt-in tenants for 2 weeks - Gradual enable via console with telemetry monitoring and automatic rollback on 'hedge_exhausted' > 5% across pools - Post-rollout: tune sampler resolution and adjust hedge_fraction per workload Known limitations and follow-ups: - Hedger currently treats all models equivalently; future work: priority-aware hedging where critical tenants get preferential loans - Sampler uses hashed tenant_group — may require downstream sampling rules to map groups to billing; action item ENG-2201 tracks that. Merge: squash merged into main after approvals (Liam, Marina) and green CI.
